title: Service quality grid and throttling orchestration spec for per-endpoint/model SLOs
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Define a machine-readable policy (the 'service quality grid') that maps per-endpoint and per-model SLIs into explicit degradation bands and automated orchestration actions: throttles, regional failover, model-variant fallback, and circuit-breaker opening. This spec standardizes SLI definitions (latency, success, model-quality regressions), error budget burn classifications, and provides decision logic for runtime hooks used by routing and autoscaler components.
background: We currently have many SLO playbooks scattered across runbooks and ad-hoc configs. Operators and platform services lack a single canonical mapping from measured SLI states to concrete runtime actions. The goal is to minimize manual intervention during partial degradation, keep critical low-latency routes alive where possible, and ensure predictable error budget consumption across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
goals: Create a canonical SLI schema for endpoints and model variants (latency quantiles, availability, quality delta against baseline prompts)
Define degradation bands (Green/Amber/Red/Critical) with numeric thresholds per SLI and per traffic tier
Specify exact orchestration actions for each band: soft-throttle, shard-level shedding, model-variant fallback, cross-region failover, circuit-breaker open/half-open behavior
Design policy primitives consumable by the routing layer, autoscaler, and console for observability and manual overrides
Provide migration guidance and a rollout plan that defaults to non-disruptive monitoring mode before enforcement
acceptance_criteria: A formal JSON/YAML schema file exists defining SLI names, types, aggregation windows, and default thresholds
Degradation bands enumerated with numeric thresholds and action hooks for each traffic tier (low/medium/high) and tenant class (free/paid/enterprise)
Routing runtime accepts the policy and emits decision logs for simulated traffic in the staging environment
An automated canary run demonstrates correct transition from Green->Amber->Red and triggers expected actions without human intervention (staging)
Console shows banded status per endpoint/model and lets operators apply manual overrides which are respected by routing within 5 seconds
implementation_notes: SLI aggregation windows: 1m/5m/1h for latency quantiles; availability measured as success ratio over same windows
Quality SLI: compute delta on a fixed promptset triggered every model rollout; treat sustained delta > 2% CTR-equivalent (configurable) as quality degradation
Error budget accounting: maintain burn-rate per endpoint and per model-variant; support borrowing with time-limited escrow
Circuit breaker semantics: use token-bucket style counters and quantile-latency thresholds; support regional weights and global override
Ensure the policy includes a safe fail-open path for enterprise customers pinned to a specific model/region
rollout_plan: Week 1: Stakeholder review (SRE/Runtime/PM/Security); finalize thresholds for two pilot endpoints (chat-low-latency, embeddings-batch)
Week 2: Implement policy parser and decision-logging in routing; deploy to staging with decision-logs only
Week 3: Run synthetic and real-traffic canaries; tune thresholds and actions; add console visualization
Week 4: Enable automated soft-throttles in production for pilot endpoints (monitor for false positives)
Week 5-6: Expand enforced endpoints incrementally; run postmortem and update spec
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive thresholds could cause cascade throttling. Mitigation: default to conservative thresholds and soft-throttle before region ejection
Risk: Quality SLI false-positives during model rollouts. Mitigation: couple quality SLI triggers with traffic-slice awareness and rollback windows
Risk: Cross-region failovers increase tail-latency for pinned tenants. Mitigation: provide policy annotations to opt out or define enterprise-safe routes
Risk: Private deployments with limited telemetry may not support full automation. Mitigation: support degraded mode where operators receive alerts but actions require manual confirmation
